artworks.title: Sacrifice at Pylos (Nestor)
artworks.description: Attic vase of Nestor's Pylian sacrifice — the household Chloris ruled as Neleus' queen and mother of Nestor, Periclymenus and Pero. The mother stays offstage; her son's court keeps her name alive.

artworks.title: Telemachus Departing from Nestor
artworks.description: Howard's Odyssey illustration: Telemachus leaves Nestor's court — the Pylian house Chloris founded with Neleus, mother of the sage who hosts Odysseus' son.

popCulture.title: Chloris (daughter of Amphion of Orchomenus)
popCulture.description: Wife of Neleus, queen of Pylos, mother of Nestor and Pero — the Chloris who survived Artemis' slaughter of the Niobids in some tellings; not the spring-nymph Flora, nor every greenfinch of the same Latin name.

popCulture.title: Nestor
popCulture.description: Chloris' most famous son — the aged counselor of the Iliad whose Pylian wisdom begins in her marriage to Neleus.

popCulture.title: Odyssey
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Homer's Telemachus visits Nestor at Pylos — Chloris' household still the first port of the son's search for news of Odysseus.
